items.readable_text:
Content:
We're used to measuring angles in degrees. However, angles can also be measured in radians (sometimes written as "[MATH: \text{rad}]"). One radian is the angle formed at the center of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ae7a9f6334b05432f18164b390c04380]

Content:
To find the number of radians in a circle, we divide the circumference of the circle by the length of a radius. We always get the same result:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{C}{r} = \dfrac{2 \pi r}{r} = 2\pi]

Content:
So, we have that

Content:
- [MATH: 360^\circ] is equivalent to [MATH: 2\pi] radians, and
- [MATH: 180^\circ] is equivalent to [MATH: \pi] radians.

Content:
As a consequence,

Content:
- to convert degrees to radians, we must multiply by [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ},] and
- to convert radians to degrees, multiply by [MATH: \dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}.]

items.title: Converting From Degrees to Radians

sections.normalized_html: An angle of [MATH: 150^\circ] is equal to how many radians?
sections.readable_text: An angle of [MATH: 150^\circ] is equal to how many radians?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To convert the measure of an angle in degrees to an equivalent measure in radians, we multiply the measure in degrees by [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ}.] This gives

[MATH: 150^{∘} ⋅ ((π)/(180^{∘}))|= (150^{∘})/(1) ⋅ ((π)/(180^{∘})); = (150^{∘})/(180^{∘}) ⋅ ((π)/(1)); = (150)/(180) ⋅ ((π)/(1)); = (15)/(18) ⋅ ((π)/(1)); = (5)/(6) ⋅ ((π)/(1)); = (5π)/(6).]

Therefore, [MATH: 150^\circ] is equivalent to [MATH: \dfrac {5\pi} {6}] radians.

Notice that when we divide [MATH: 150^\circ] by [MATH: 180^\circ,] we can drop the degree [MATH: (\phantom{.}^\circ)] symbol.

sections.normalized_html: What is the angle of [MATH: \dfrac{2 \pi} 3] radians in degrees?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To convert the measure of an angle in radians to an equivalent measure in degrees, we multiply the measure in radians by [MATH: \dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}.] This gives

[MATH: ((2π)/(3)) ⋅ ((180^{∘})/(π))|= (2 ⋅ 180^{∘} ⋅ π)/(3 ⋅ π); = (360^{∘}π)/(3π); = (360^{∘}π)/(3π); = (360^{∘})/(3); = 120^{∘}.]

Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{2 \pi} 3] is equivalent to [MATH: 120^\circ.]
